learning_outcomes.text: Develop their ability to imagine ideal geometric forms and relate them mentally.
Learn the elements of standardization and usual representation principles in engineering.
Acquire the necessary skills to generate graphic representations, from quick sketches to detailed manufacturing plans.
Understand the role of graphic expression in the global scope of technical communication in Engineering.
Understand the difference between ideal and real geometry of objects.
Exercise acquired skills as a means of concretizing and communicating their own spatial creativity.
Understand the functioning of a mechanical assembly and correctly represent the parts of any assembly following representation standards.
Correctly dimension any part of a mechanical assembly, defining, if necessary, the tolerances for its correct functioning.
Know the techniques for modeling mechanical parts and assemblies by computer and generating standardized technical drawings.
Model mechanical parts or assemblies with Computer-Aided Engineering tools and perform mechanical calculation by the finite element method.
Model mechanical parts or assemblies with Computer-Aided Engineering tools and perform stationary and transient thermal simulations by the finite element method.
Model a mechanical assembly with Computer-Aided Engineering tools and perform kinematic and dynamic simulation of the associated mechanism.
Model mechanical parts or assemblies with Computer-Aided Engineering tools and perform the simulation of their manufacturing process.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Representation techniques in Engineering: Dihedral System, Standardized Views and Axonometric System (Isometric).
Standardization in industry and industrial drawing. Standardized paper formats and presentation of graphic elements on drawing sheets.
Assembly drawings, exploded perspective and dimensioned detail drawings.
Threaded joints. Elements of a thread. Profiles, representation and dimensioning.
Shafts and axles. Keys and splines.
Gear: calculation, types, representation and dimensioning.
Welding: types of joints, representation and designation.
Dimensional tolerances and fits. Geometric tolerances. Surface finishes.
3D CAD. CGS. Parametric CAD: Catia (in laboratory practices).
teaching_methods: Classroom presentations of concepts and problem solving
assessment_rules: Student performance is graded on a numerical scale from 0 to 10 with one decimal: 0-4.9 (Fail), 5.0-6.9 (Pass), 7.0-8.9 (Notable), 9.0-10 (Outstanding). A 'Matrícula de Honor' is awarded for grades 9.0 or higher, limited to 5% of enrolled students or one if fewer than 20 students. Continuous evaluation comprises four controls, each contributing 25% to the theoretical-practical part, and laboratory practices which contribute 30% to the total grade. The theoretical-practical part constitutes 70% of the final grade, and a minimum of 3 is required in each control. Tasks and exercises can add up to 1 extra point to the theoretical-practical score. In ordinary and extraordinary resit calls, if continuous evaluation is not passed, a final exam covering the theoretical-practical part (70% of final grade) is taken, and the laboratory grade (30%) from continuous evaluation is retained or assigned 0 if not obtained.
